hold.clamp: hand snug, then quarter turn; confirm seating and rail engagement
hold.note: Grip the full-thickness rails on the matched riser pair plus 1/2 in parallels. Risers: two O1 bars 76.2 long (along the jaws) x 63.5 wide x 25.4 high, cut from one bought 1 x 2-1/2 in precision-ground O1 flat bar, annealed, so their heights match within 0.01. Make them before S1: bandsaw two pieces 78 long, 4/6 bi-metal blade on the 120 ft/min belt step, dry (MH 27th p.1142: O-1 200 fpm with coolant, 30-50% less dry); on the PM-30MV, each piece on end in the vise, gripped across its ground faces with 40 above the jaws, face the top end with the 1/2 in 2-flute end mill (tools.endmills-lms-6784) in 6 mm step-overs at 340-380 rpm, 0.001 in/tooth, 0.25 mm a pass (MH 27th Table 12 p.1049, O1 at 175-225 HB: HSS end milling 50 fpm, 382 rpm on the 1/2 in; Table 15a p.1054 tool-steel rows .001-.002 in/tooth); reverse it, a square against the faced end, and face the other end to 76.2 the same way; file the burrs. Check the pair together on the surface plate with the test indicator before use. Stand both on the vise floor, ground faces up and down, centred X -40 and X +40, Y 4.5, with a 3.8 gap between them at X 0; the 63.5 width fits between the 65 mm closed jaws. Stand the two parallels on the risers, wholly on both bars, under the retained rails at Y -25.5 and Y 34.5. Seat the aluminium L's seat face on the tapped face, its finger toward the front and its arm top flush with the base top (a straightedge across both), and fit the M6 x 16 SHCS through the lug into the tap; tighten it, then switch the base on. Once op 27 releases the outline, the two closing straps take its cut load by friction on face B; the hardened diamond pin is an in-process orientation locator only, not datum C, and takes no clamp or cut load. Keep every clamp tight until op 27 is complete and the cutter is retracted. The pin's clearance in the rod hole (S2 op 34 process hold) is part of the orientation budget.
hold.release: CAPACITY CHECK (example data), for the op 27 release; the traveler does not print it (issue #158). Cut force, MH 27th pp.1086-1088, Pc = Kp C Q W: Kp 2.13 kW per cm3/s (Table 3b p.1086, plain carbon steels 160-180 HB, a harder band than the 1018 part's); C 1.70 (Table 4 p.1087, the 0.02 mm row, under the declared 0.025 mm/tooth chip load); W 1.10 (Table 5 p.1087, end milling); Q = fm w d / 60000 = 140 x 6.35 x 0.625 / 60000 = 0.00926 cm3/s (Table 7 p.1088: 140 mm/min = 1400 rpm x 4 flutes x 0.025, a full 6.35 slot, one 0.625 level); Pc = 36.9 W; at V = pi x 6.35 x 1400 = 27.9 m/min the full-slot force is 79.2 N, and 158.5 N with a safety factor of 2. Lever, with no credit for the shoulder screw, the washer or the pin: that force at the path point farthest from the pivot (150.75) puts (70 + 150.75) / 140 = 1.577 of it on the nearer strap: 250 N. Friction, MH 27th p.158: steel on steel with oil once sliding starts, 0.03, on two faces at each toe (strap on face B, face A on the O1 pad): 0.06 of the toe force, so the toe needs 250 / 0.06 = 4170 N. Strap: toe force = stud tension x (63.27 - 40.00) / 63.27. T = K F d (MH 27th p.1495, K 0.2 for the zinc-plated stud, d 0.375 in): 23 N·m gives 12.07 kN stud tension and 4440 N at the toe, 266 N of friction, 2.13 times the unfactored 125 N. Stud: 12.07 kN on the 0.0775 in2 (50.0 mm2) stress area of 3/8-16 (Table 4a p.1763) is 241 MPa, under the SAE Grade 2 proof of 55 ksi (379 MPa, p.1508) and the 14.2 kN reusable preload 0.75 At Sp of p.1495. Beam at the stud hole: 4440 x 40.00 = 177.6 N·m on (38.1 - 11.1) x 16.0^2 / 6 = 1152 mm3 is 154 MPa, 2.24 times under the 50 ksi (345 MPa) minimum yield of cold-drawn 1018 over 1-1/4 to 2 in (Table 10 p.464); the nose at x 15 (38.1 x 13.28) carries 66.6 N·m at 60 MPa. DO NOT COMBINE LEVELS: two levels at once double the force and leave 1.07 times the unfactored load instead of 2.13; three slide the part.

inspection_method: Inspection box (buy and adapt before S4; example dimensions, plausible, not measured): a bought Suburban BXP-050505-G 127 mm cast-iron box parallel, 11/16 in (17.46) walls round one vertical through core. Mark its right side. AUTHOR'S CHOICE: the box is sold square within 0.0083 per 100, short of the 0.003 per 100 this check needs, so its actual base-to-right squareness is measured by reversal (steps 5 and 6) and the view-2 reading is corrected for it (step 16).

Box windows, milled on the PM-30MV with light cuts, the box held by toe clamps on parallels, never in the vise: two 32 x 24 clamp windows through the left wall, 16.0 to 48.0 behind the front face, at 40 to 64 and 88 to 112 above the base; one 80 x 80 access window in the back wall, 23.5 from the left face and the base. Add only dimensioned work: only the taps cut the front face. Each window: drill a 7/16 start hole (tools.drill-index-115) at a corner at 500-600 rpm, 0.15 mm/rev, then mill it out with the 3/8 in 4-flute end mill (tools.endmills-lms-6784) at 600-700 rpm, 0.001 in/tooth, 1.0 mm a pass (MH 27th Table 14 p.1052, gray cast iron, taken as ASTM Class 30, 190-220 HB: HSS end milling 70 fpm; Table 15a p.1054 gray cast iron .001 in/tooth for a 1/4-1/2 in cutter at .050 in depth; Table 20 p.1068: HSS drilling 80 fpm, 700 rpm on the 7/16 in, held lower for the interrupted break-through). Drill #29 (tools.drill-index-115) at 1800-2200 rpm, 0.05 mm/rev (Table 20 p.1068: 80 fpm, 2250 rpm on the #29; p.1060: .001-.003 in/rev under 1/8 in) and tap two #8-32 holes 10.0 full thread (#29 drill 12.0 deep) by hand in the front face, 10.00 and 30.00 from the left face, 6.35 ±0.10 above the base.

C stop bar (make before S4; example dimensions, plausible, not measured): hardened O1 (58-62 HRC), lapped top and bottom to 12.700 ±0.003, parallel within 0.002, no nicks, burrs or stamping on the top face, on the front face at its left end, projecting 12.7 forward; the whole route, steps (a) to (g), follows. From a bought 1/2 x 1/2 x 18 in precision-ground O1 flat bar (Abrams Industries 102060), annealed (175-225 HB): (a) bandsaw 42 off with the 4/6 bi-metal blade on the 120 ft/min belt step, dry (MH 27th p.1142: O-1 200 fpm with coolant, 30-50% less dry). (b) PM-30MV, bar in the vise on parallels: mill both ends square to 40.0 with the 3/8 in 4-flute end mill (tools.endmills-lms-6784) at 450-500 rpm, 0.001 in/tooth, 0.5 mm a pass (MH 27th Table 12 p.1049, O1 at 175-225 HB: HSS end milling 50 fpm, 509 rpm on the 3/8 in; Table 15a p.1054 tool-steel rows .001-.002 in/tooth). (c) Same vise, a 40 x 12.7 side face up, X/Y picked up with the edge finder from the left end and the fixed-jaw side: centre drill, then drill #9 (0.196 in, 4.98) through at 10.0 and 30.0 from the left end on the face's centre line at 800-875 rpm, 0.05 mm/rev (MH 27th Table 18 p.1066, O1 at 175-225 HB: HSS drilling 45 fpm, 877 rpm on the #9; feed inside p.1060's .001-.003 in/rev for that size), and counterbore each Ø5/16 (7.94) x 4.8 deep with the 5/16 in 2-flute end mill at 550-600 rpm, a light quill plunge to the stop (Table 12 p.1049: 50 fpm, 611 rpm on the 5/16 in). (d) Harden (O1, torch, oil quench): coat the bar with ATP-641 anti-scale, heat it in the fire-brick chamber with the TS8000 torch (equalise at dull red, then an even cherry red one shade past non-magnetic on the pickup magnet, hold about 5 min), quench it moving in warm Park's AAA oil in the lidded M2A1 can and pull it hand-warm. (e) Temper at once: 400 °F for 2 h, air cool, twice, in the tempering oven checked with the oven thermometer (MH 27th p.496 Table 9: about Rc 60). (f) Lap. The finishing allowance is the bought bar's own oversize: before step (a), micrometer the 18 in bar every 25 and saw the 42 piece from a stretch reading 12.712-12.725, leaving 0.006-0.012 a side to lap off scale, skin and quench distortion; if no stretch reads 12.712, do not use the bar. Lap the bottom first on the cast-iron lap plate with 400 then 800 compound and kerosene, figure-8 strokes, turning the bar end for end every 20 strokes, until the whole face is an even grey. Then lap the top the same way, comparing it every few strokes on the granite against the 12.70 gauge-block stack (11.5 + 1.20) with the 1 µm test indicator at both ends and the middle, down to 12.700 ±0.003. Stress-relief temper at 350 °F for 1 h (AUTHOR'S CHOICE: under the 400 °F temper, so it cannot soften the bar), then give the top a final light 800 lap. (g) Check and record: thickness 12.700 ±0.003 at both ends and the middle, by the gauge-block comparison; parallelism within 0.002, the highest of those three readings less the lowest; hardness 58-62 HRC with the hardness files on a lapped face (the 55 file skates, the 60 file skates or barely bites); no nicks, burrs or stamping on the top face. Box holes, after the windows are milled: stand the box and the bar together on the granite, the bar pressed to the front face at its left end, and spot the front face through both bar holes with the #9 drill turned by hand; then, box on its base on parallels under toe clamps on the PM-30MV, drill #29 (0.136 in; MH 27th Table 4 p.1934) with the quill stop set so the tool tip stops 13.0 into the 17.46 front wall (full Ø to 12.0) at 1800-2200 rpm, 0.05 mm/rev (MH 27th Table 20 p.1068, gray cast iron: HSS drilling 80 fpm, 2247 rpm on the #29), and tap #8-32 UNC-2B by hand, the tools.taps-unc-hand/8-32-plug then the tools.taps-unc-hand/8-32-bottoming to 10.0 full thread. Fit: stand the box and the bar together on the granite, bar pressed to the front face, and tighten its two #8-32 x 5/8 in cap screws (about 8.0 of thread in the wall): its underside is then flush with the base and its lapped top 12.70 above it. No dowels.
Equilibrate the part, the box, the gauge pins and the gauge blocks on the granite surface plate (gauges.granite-surface-plate) at 20 ±1 °C.

Box squareness by reversal (each inspection session; never before the windows are milled), on the granite surface plate (gauges.granite-surface-plate), the 1 µm test indicator on the height gauge, a higher contact reading positive: (a) box on its base, indicator over the top face at one slider setting: read 10 in from the left face and 10 in from the right side; p = (right - left) x 100 / 107 = {p}. (b) Right side toward the gauge: read the right side at 10 and at 110 above the granite, moving only the slider; s1 = reading at 110 - reading at 10 = {s1}. (c) Roll the box over onto its top face about the axis square to the right side, so the right side still faces the gauge, and repeat (b): s2 = {s2}.

Calculate: E_box = (s1 - s2 - p) / 2 = {E_box} per 100 (positive: the right side's top stands out past its foot, so the base-to-right angle is over 90°). The height-gauge column's own lean is in both s1 and s2 and cancels.
Push the largest freely passing gauge pin through bore A and through the rod hole; copy the actual diameters marked on the pins: {pin A Ø} {rod pin Ø}.

Fixed-C contact: stand the box on its base, front face toward you. Lay strap datum B (the upper strap face) flat on the front face, rod end down, with the A axis within 5 of the box's left edge, and lower the part until land C (the +X tip land) sits on the stop bar's lapped top; the hub stands clear above the box. Clamp B finger-light with two 3 in toolmaker's parallel clamps through the left windows, without bending or clamping the free span. Keep this C contact and these clamps unchanged through step 14.

Reading a pin: wring a gauge-block stack of known length beside the pin's top, zero the 1 µm test indicator on the stack, then sweep the pin crown at the same height-gauge setting and read the deviation; a higher contact must read positive. Pin-centre height = stack length + deviation - pin radius. The height gauge only carries the indicator; do not use its scale.
View 1, box on its base with C down on the bar (hub pin about 132.4 above the rod pin): read each pin within 2 of an accessible bore face: hub-centre height {H1}, rod-centre height {R1}.

Lean check, view 1: read the hub pin at its accessible mouth {mouth 1} and 10 farther out {out 1}. If they differ by more than 0.005, or B cannot seat without leaning the pin, the readings are not valid: reseat from step 8 and repeat; if it persists, stop and report.

View 2: without unclamping the part or losing C contact, tip the whole box a quarter turn clockwise as you face its front, onto its marked right side (rod pin now about 15.8 below the hub pin). Read both pins the same way: hub-centre height {H2}, rod-centre height {R2}.

Reseat check: gently press the non-rod tip toward the stop bar, release, and read both pins again: hub {H3}, rod {R3}. If H3 - R3 and H2 - R2 differ by more than 0.002, the seating did not repeat: reseat from step 8 and redo both views.
Lean check, view 2, as in step 11: {mouth 2} {out 2}.
Calculate: X = H1 - R1 = {X}; Y = H3 - R3 = {Y}.

Calculate: Y corrected = Y - E_box x X / 100 = {Y corrected}. View 2 reads square to the right side, which leans E_box per 100 from square to the base, so over the X lever between the pins it adds E_box x X / 100 to Y.

Calculate: position Ø = 2 × √((X - 132.391)² + (Y corrected - 15.843)²) = {position Ø}; compare it with the drawing limit on the op row (RFS, no bonus). 132.391 and 15.843 are the CAD nominals for this inspection set-up, not the milling X/Y.
